## Week 5 – OpenLoom (ESP32 History Flashcard Device)

### What I worked on
OpenLoom is a pocket History flashcard device built around an ESP32. It has an OLED screen, 2 buttons (next / reveal) and a buzzer for feedback. This session I [wired up the OLED and buttons / wrote the card-flip logic / tested the buzzer / cleaned up the repo].

### What I built
- [Show the question on the OLED and reveal the answer with a button press]
- [Button debouncing so one press equals one action]
- [Buzzer beep on reveal / next card]
- [Repo checks all passing on GitHub]

### What broke and how I fixed it
- [Problem, e.g. OLED stayed blank → I had the wrong I2C address, fixed it after scanning]
- [Problem, e.g. buttons triggered twice → added a debounce delay]

### What's next
- [Add more History cards (topics from my B.A. course)]
- [Add a score / streak counter]
- [Take final photos of the device and finish the README]
